title: Leveraging tails for adaptation
summary: We consider contraction of Bayesian posterior distributions in nonparametric settings where coefficients of a function over a basis or dictionary are given priors with $p$--exponential tails, including Laplace tails $(p=1)$ and heavier tails $(p<1)$. It is shown that contraction rates improve as $p$ decreases and that full adaptation to smoothness, up to logarithmic factors, is obtained in an appropriate $p\to 0$ regime.
